clue.text: Friends, say, in favour of the metric system?

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
a unit belonging to the metric system, British spelling

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Friends gang would back going metric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' flags Friends as an example: the sitcom is one instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends was a television show, and a scheduled broadcast show is called a programme in British spelling.

clue.text: Layer upon layer of egg mayonnaise finally eaten by parents

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: surface padding that keeps the kitchen picture going
the final letter of mayonnaise
fathers are parents

explanation.surface: A recipe describes building up stacked layers of egg mayonnaise that the parents then eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A layer is a hen, a bird that lays eggs, and its plumage sits layer upon layer on it; 'egg' keeps the kitchen picture going. E goes inside FATHERS for FEATHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A laying hen is covered in overlapping plumage, so the definition describes a bird's coat lying on a layer.

clue.text: Notorious Transylvanian doctor pursued by a copper north of Los Angeles

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the usual abbreviation for the Californian city

explanation.surface: A shady Transylvanian medic is chased by a policeman somewhere above Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is the metal. In a down clue 'north of' puts CU above LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire count came from Transylvania and is that region's most infamous fictional resident.

clue.text: Close to Oldham, an English city

definitions.text: Close to Oldham, an English city

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the closing letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Oldham
taken as written
Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire

explanation.surface: A plain gazetteer entry for a large city lying beside Oldham.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the answer, since Oldham is a town on the edge of Greater Manchester; read in pieces it builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a major city in northwest England whose outskirts adjoin the town of Oldham.

clue.text: Place with dodgy loos

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound and not as it should be, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about somewhere whose toilets are unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital city is a location, so it counts as an example of a geographical spot.

clue.text: Online photograph TikToker's first taken for foodie

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows
a letter taken away is removed from the longer word

blocks.note: e- is the prefix for electronic or online things
a photograph is a picture
the opening letter of TikToker

explanation.surface: A TikTok influencer snaps a picture of their dinner for an audience of food lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus PICTURE gives E-PICTURE, an online photograph; removing its T leaves EPICURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to refined eating and drinking, which is what a foodie is.

clue.text: Monkey bar broken by short kick

indicators.note: a thing broken by another has that other thing pushed into its middle
short means cut off before the end, so a last letter goes

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
BOOT, a kick, lacking its final letter

explanation.surface: A drinker kicks at a pub bar and smashes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as the pub counter, but here it is a verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboons are large African primates with dog-like muzzles, a kind of Old World monkey.

clue.text: Boxer at risk of toppling over?

blocks.note: first meaning: the fictional prizefighter Balboa of the film series
second meaning: unsteady, wobbly

explanation.surface: A punch-drunk fighter is about to keel over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Balboa is Sylvester Stallone's famous boxer, and something rocky is unstable and liable to fall.

clue.text: Money invested in Sussex town's bakery products

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Rye is a town in East Sussex, plus the possessive S
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash has been put into a local business in a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, England; the possessive 's is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaves made with rye flour are things a bakery sells, so plural rye breads are bakery goods.

clue.text: Gently turning about a copper coin

indicators.note: turning round makes the following string face the other way

blocks.note: on means about, concerning
taken as written
1P, one penny, is a copper coin; the digit 1 stands for I

explanation.surface: Someone is gently spinning a penny on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: ON + A + 1P reads ONAIP, and reversed this gives PIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction meaning to play softly, so it is the musicians' word for quietly.

clue.text: Understand only a small extract from strange text

indicators.note: an extract is a piece lifted out, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A reader grasps just a fragment of a baffling passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a joke or idea is to grasp it, an informal synonym for comprehending.

clue.text: Swiss home of winger making regular appearances

definitions.text: Swiss home of winger making regular appearances

blocks.note: surface reading: a Swiss house where some sportsman or bird lives
setter's reading: a timepiece from Switzerland whose wooden bird pops out on the hour

explanation.surface: A footballer playing as a winger keeps turning up at his Swiss house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird, and its regular appearances are hourly ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic Black Forest and Swiss souvenir timepiece houses a model bird that emerges and calls at each hour.

clue.text: Nipple rings are worn by leads in Eugene Onegin, Lohengrin and Aida

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters
a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the initials of the four title words

explanation.surface: Opera singers in leading roles are sporting nipple piercings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like the starring singers, but means the first letters of each opera name.
explanation.definitionFit: The areola is the pigmented circle of skin surrounding a nipple; areolae is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Police chief holding one end of rubber thing with unknown length

indicators.note: one end of a word is its first or last letter, here the first
holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Sting was the frontman of the band The Police
the opening letter of rubber

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is holding a rubber item of uncertain length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police chief' suggests a constable's boss, but it is the singer who led The Police. The definition plays on the saying 'how long is a piece of string?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhetorical question about how long a piece of twine is means its length cannot be known.

clue.text: Pet with small gold/green tail

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sage is a greyish-green colour
to tail someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A little pet animal has a tail coloured gold and green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like part of the pet but is a verb meaning follow. Sausage dog is the British informal name for a dachshund.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund, nicknamed for its long low body, is a breed commonly kept as a household companion animal.

clue.text: Give smaller portions to United defender when injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football club cuts a player's meals after he gets hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To underfeed someone is to provide them with too little nourishment, serving meals that are too small.

clue.text: Something served in Grandma's house?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A question about what dish gets dished up at Grandma's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato, served as a side dish with bangers or pies, is food put on a plate.

clue.text: Sealed by you in Senegal, a letter from abroad

indicators.note: something sealed by another is closed up inside it

blocks.note: tu is French for you, and French is Senegal's official language
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Senegal arrives sealed by you.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside TU. The definition 'a letter' is shared: 'a' also gives A in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: See 25
Doughnut artist put doughnuts on another doughnut to create noted work

blocks.note: a doughnut ring is shaped like the letter O
RA is a Royal Academician
tori, plural of torus, is the geometers' name for doughnut shapes
a second ring shape

explanation.surface: A pastry-loving painter stacks doughnut upon doughnut to make a creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes. A torus is the mathematical doughnut shape, plural tori.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical composition for choir and soloists, a work written in notes.

clue.text: A trifle disintegrating in thong

indicators.note: something disintegrating falls apart, so these letters break up and re-form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dessert is falling apart inside someone's flimsy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' suggests the custard pudding, but means something of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a matter of little consequence, and nothing is something unimportant, as in 'it's nothing'.

clue.text: Was the drink left by this type of dish?

definitions.text: Was the drink left by this type of dish?

blocks.clueFragment: Was the drink left by this
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about a beverage left beside a plate
setter's reading: the drink is the ocean, and its catch is what the ocean leaves behind

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a drink was left next to a particular dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the ocean, so the clue asks for food the ocean leaves us.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and shellfish come from the ocean, which slang calls the drink, so dishes of them are marine fare.

clue.text: Our colonel, leading in khaki?

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, placed in front
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our army colonel is out in front, dressed in khaki uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks khaki as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow shade, one example of a hue or tint.

clue.text: Kill and kill again, causing upset

blocks.note: to off someone is slang for to murder them
to end someone is to kill them, a second synonym

explanation.surface: A double murder causes distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend people is to hurt their feelings or annoy them, the verb sense of making someone upset.

clue.text: Great Victorian industrialist manufacturing plastic

blocks.note: ace means excellent
Henry Tate, the sugar refiner who founded the Tate gallery

explanation.surface: A celebrated Victorian businessman is making plastic goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate was the 19th-century British sugar magnate behind the Tate Gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate is a synthetic material used for film and packaging, a kind of plastic.

definitions.note: 1-down, PROGRAMME: Countdown is a long-running British TV quiz show

blocks.note: 3-down is DRACULA, who is a count
2-down is FEATHERS, and fine feathers are down

explanation.surface: Mission control reads out the final seconds before a launch, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are not a countdown but cross-references to 3-down, 2-down and 1-down; the whole clue also describes the answer. Countdown is a British daytime TV words-and-numbers game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Countdown is a long-running Channel 4 game show, so it is a television programme.

clue.text: Mass-produced article seen amongst rotten, decomposing flesh

a thing seen amongst others sits in the middle of them

blocks.note: food that has gone off is rotten
the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome find of an item lying in rotting meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item but is the grammar term for a word like 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods taken straight from a shop's stock rather than custom-made are standard factory items, which is the sense here.

clue.text: ...blast off!" Abandon the first part of launch attempt

indicators.note: the first part of a word here is just its opening letter
abandoning something leaves it out of the word
off means gone wrong or awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of launch

explanation.surface: Continuing 25's countdown, a rocket launch is called off.

explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is an informal idiom for trying it, so a stab is a go or try.

clue.text: After 20, a fellow is a fool

blocks.note: 20-down is NOTHING, and nothing is zero, O
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone is called an idiot in the aftermath of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After 20' starts the word with what 20-down gives: nothing, which is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, and a fool is likewise someone lacking sense.

clue.text: Head of Nike's in love with new fabric

blocks.note: the opening letter of Nike
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Nike' sounds like the company's chief executive but means just its first letter.

clue.text: Express regret when first post office account is essentially discredited

standard abbreviation

taken as written
the central letter of discredited
